note: SAME DEPOSIT AND SAME METHOD AS batch_202's gilbert_meta_73, so the reasoning there applies here too. The renaming happened upstream of this repo -- data/gilbert_hte/postprocessing.R points at an external 'gilbert_share/06 IL-HTE Econ/analysis/' -- so the correspondence was verified against the data rather than read off a script. ITEM TEXT IS THE TASK DESCRIPTION, NOT A LITERAL ITEM, and that is deliberate rather than a gap: the deposit ships FOUR parallel forms whose content differs, and the live table records no form, so no literal item is a property of an item code. The visible consequence is that item_text repeats across a task family. resp is 0/1 and the deposit publishes no value labels for these variables, so option_text is blank; that 1 means correct follows from makedata.do recoding 9 to 0 and summing the items into test scores, and is recorded in the public note as an inference rather than a transcription. VERIFICATION: 12 of the 33 codes are wave-restricted by the dictionary and all 12 hold in the data -- the nine baseline-only codes (comp1-comp4 comprehension, and the six let_fill boxes) appear at wave 0 alone, and the three endline-only word_dic codes appear at 0.5 and 1 only. The remaining 21 span all three waves as the dictionary implies. That the baseline and endline forms differ in content is itself the finding: the baseline form carried comprehension and letter-filling tasks that the endline forms dropped, and the endline forms added word dictation. A NOTE ON WHAT THESE ITEMS ARE: several are picture-dependent -- matpic ('Encircle the word which matches with the picture'), obj_name ('Look at the picture and write the name of the object') and writpic ('Look at the picture, and write the word') -- so even with a single form there would be no transcribable stem beyond the task, only an image. The task description is the whole of the available text for those nine items regardless of the parallel-forms problem.

VERIFICATION AND A SOURCE ERROR IT FOUND. The wave test is weak on this table -- 19 of its 20 codes are defined in all three waves, so only one code is discriminating -- and that one code exposed a TYPO IN THE DICTIONARY rather than a problem with the mapping. mathwrit_std12_add2d_b is listed with b_ and e2_ prefixes but no e1_, which would mean it was not administered at midline; the data has it at midline. The cause is visible in the sheet: 'Math Aser & Written test-End1' row 8b gives the variable name as e1_mathwrit_std12_add2d_a, duplicating row 8a, while that row's own question label correctly reads 'q8_b Addition-two digit'. It cannot affect what ships: rows 8a and 8b carry the identical task description, 'Addition-two digit'.

source_ref: CC0 Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/DIU6BU (Bateman et al., STOPTHEBURN trial), single file 'STOPTHEBURN Data.xlsx' -- a REDCap export whose 'Survey Data' sheet carries the administered item wording as column headers (cols 20-56) and the administered option labels as cell values. Protocol paper: Bateman et al. 2020, 'Death Cafes for prevention of burnout in intensive care unit employees: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial (STOPTHEBURN)', Trials 21:1019, doi:10.1186/s13063-020-04929-4, CC BY 4.0 (PMC7729694) -- names the three instruments, gives the 2-week reference period for PHQ-8/GAD-7, gives the four survey timepoints, and gives the MBI subscale cut-scores used above to fix the subscale sizes. Rights source for the MBI: Mind Garden's own permissions page, which requires a purchased License to Administer and states that 'Only three sample items from this instrument may be included in your thesis or dissertation, and any other use must receive prior written permission from Mind Garden', plus a per-page copyright notice requirement.
note: PARTIAL SHIP ON RIGHTS GROUNDS: 15 of 37 items carry item_text, 22 do not. The split is exactly by instrument and it is visible in the data before any document is read, because the two blocks use different response ranges -- the 15 PHQ-8/GAD-7 items run 0-3 and the 22 MBI items run 0-6. WHY THE 22 ARE WITHHELD: the MBI-HSS is commercially published by Mind Garden and the restriction is quotable on both of Ben's block criteria at once -- a purchased License to Administer is required (a fee), and 'any other use must receive prior written permission from Mind Garden' (an explicit permission-required clause). Under Ben's 2026-09-06 ruling ('let's err on the side of not having things. so do not host') the item wording is not hosted. Note this differs from the standing 'source cannot share' exclusion in SKILL.md: this source DID share -- the depositors published all 22 MBI items as CC0 column headers -- so the bar is IRW's own conservatism about republishing a licensed instrument, not a publisher's refusal to the study team. WHY THE MBI ANCHORS DO SHIP WHILE THE ITEMS DO NOT, AND HOW TO REVERSE THAT IN ONE STEP: option_text for the MBI block is the 7-point frequency scale (Never / A few times a year or less / Once a month or less / A few times a month / Once a week / A few times a week / Every day). It ships for three reasons -- it is the answer format rather than item content, it was published in Maslach & Jackson's original 1981 journal article and is restated in this study's own CC BY protocol, and without it the resp column for 22 of 37 items is uninterpretable, which is the one thing an itemtext table exists to prevent. This is a judgement call inside Ben's ruling rather than something the ruling settles, so it is isolated for easy reversal: blanking option_text on section_id gilbert_meta_45_3 removes it and nothing else. ESCALATE TO BEN -- WITHHOLDING item_text HERE PROTECTS NOTHING. The live IRW item codes ARE the MBI item wording in snake_case: i_feel_burned_out_from_my_work, ive_become_more_callous_toward_people_since_i_took_this_job, i_dont_really_care_what_happens_to_some_patients, and 19 more. All 22 are already published verbatim in the gilbert_meta_45 RESPONSE table and are recoverable by anyone who reads a code, entirely independently of itemtext. The Prime Commandment requires all 37 codes to ship for the join to work, so the exposure cannot be closed from this side at all -- it would take a decision about the response table's item codes, which is outside this skill. The blank item_text column here should be read as IRW declining to ADD a hosted copy, not as the wording being unavailable. Same question likely applies to any other MBI table in the gilbert_meta family. REVERSE CODING (applies to interpreting resp, and it is not obvious from the codes): the 8 Personal Accomplishment items are reverse-coded in the live data relative to what respondents saw, so 'Never' maps to resp 6 and 'Every day' to resp 0 on those items, and high resp means more burnout uniformly across all 22 MBI items. This is not an assumption -- it is what makes the 851-cell reproduction close exactly, and the paper's own <33/48 cut-score independently fixes PA at 8 items. The recode happened upstream of this repo: there is no data/gilbert_meta_45 script, the table comes in through the gilbert_hte meta-analysis pipeline. correct_response is empty throughout: all three instruments are self-report frequency ratings with no key. section_prompt is empty because the REDCap export carries none. instructions is empty for the MBI block, since the MBI's own instruction paragraph is Mind Garden text and falls under the same withholding as the items.
public_note: Thirty-seven items across three instruments, administered at four timepoints (wave 0 = baseline, 1 = 1 month, 2 = 3 months, 3 = 6 months). The instruments are separated by response range: the PHQ-8 (8 items) and GAD-7 (7 items) run 0-3, and the Maslach Burnout Inventory - Human Services Survey (22 items) runs 0-6. ITEM TEXT IS WITHHELD FOR THE 22 MBI ITEMS. The MBI is commercially licensed by Mind Garden, which requires a purchased License to Administer and prior written permission for other uses, so IRW does not host the wording. The MBI response anchors are provided, since the resp column is otherwise uninterpretable. Item text for the 15 PHQ-8 and GAD-7 items is the wording administered, taken from the study's own CC0 deposit; both instruments are free to reproduce. IMPORTANT FOR ANYONE SCORING THE MBI: the 8 Personal Accomplishment items are ALREADY REVERSE-CODED in this table. Higher resp means more burnout on all 22 MBI items, which is the opposite of the direction respondents answered in for those 8. Do not reverse them again. The mapping between each item's response options and its resp values is given per item in this table and reflects the reversal. The 'Not at all' anchor is spelled '(0-1 day)' on the PHQ-8 and '(0-1 days)' on the GAD-7; that difference is in the study's own survey forms and is transcribed as found. The whole table was verified by reproducing every one of its 851 item-by-response-by-wave cell counts exactly from the deposit.
